dismissals.because: apps/api/test/accounts.integration.spec.ts:204 The Google start and callback flow is proven at the API layer with a fake Google issuer: a new person from /circles/join/google is redirected to /onboarding?returnTo=%2Fcircles%2Fjoin%2Fgoogle, and a returning member to the invite (line 215). The browser test covers the web half (pending session goes to onboarding and returns to the invite); the browser suite has no fake Google issuer and adding one is shared test configuration outside this part.

apps/api/test/circles-join.integration.spec.ts:148 Simultaneous joins are enforced and proven by the API against the real database: overlapping joins stop at 20 circles per member (line 148) and at 100 members (line 260). This part is the web invite page and owns no server logic; the browser test covers how the page shows the refusals.

findings.body: The browser test reads the Google link’s return path, then calls `test-auth/sign-in` and installs the session cookie directly. It never follows the app’s Google start and callback flow. A callback that loses the invite path would still pass this test.
findings.title: Not done: invite sign-in and onboarding return test

findings.body: The test fills the circle through sequential joins. It does not overlap join requests at either the 100-member or 20-circle boundary, so it would pass if simultaneous admissions exceeded either limit.
findings.title: Not done: concurrent join limit test

findings.body: After Join, the test checks membership but never verifies that exactly one usage event records the member and circle. It also never forces event recording to fail and checks that the join remains committed while that event is uncounted. Both required behaviours could break while this test passes.
findings.title: Not done: join usage event test

findings.body: The branch adds a task status file outside both permitted paths. The file is unnecessary for the invite page or its tests.
findings.title: Remove the task status file outside the allowed paths
